newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls decision rejecting claims of cartel practices.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls decision rejecting claims of cartel practices.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance has told the European Commission to take another look at allegations of cartel practices between importers of Japanese cars into France.

The court annulled in part a Commission decision which rejected complaints from French parallel importers of Japanese cars that they were squeezed out of the market by anti- competitive practices of authorized importers of Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Mazda and Mitsubishi.

Five parallel importers of Japanese cars into France complained to the Commission, first in 1985, that Japanese car dealerships acted in concert with the French government to limit the number of Japanese cars sold in France.
The Commission rejected the claims in a 1994 decision, finding the limit placed on the number of Japanese cars sold in France was the result of public policy, not cartel practices.
The court told the Commission it did not do enough research to determine if the undertakings at issue had "any margin of autonomy" in setting the limits of Japanese cars sold in France.

"In the absence of any binding regulatory provision imposing the conduct at issue, the court considers that the Commission is entitled to reject the complaints for want of autonomy on the part of the undertakings in question only if it appears on the basis of objective, relevant and consistent evidence that that conduct was unilaterally imposed upon them by the national authorities through the exercise of irresistible pressures...," the court said.

In finding the Commission did not base the contested decision on objective, relevant and consistent evidence such as to show that the French authorities unilaterally brought irresistible pressures to bear on the undertakings, the court said the Commission made a manifest error in assessing the facts.
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Competition - Obligations with regard to the investigation of complaints - Legality of grounds for rejection - Manifest error of assessment - Statement of reasons"
18 September 1996
Case T-387/94
Asia Motor France SA, Jean-Michel Cesbron, Monin Automobiles SA, Europe Auto Service (EAS) SA, SA Somaco SARL, applicants
v
Commission of the European Communities, defendant

Application for the annulment of the Commission's decision of 13 October 1994 rejecting the applicants' complaints relating to cartel practices alleged to be contrary to article 85 of the EEC Treaty, and for compensation for the damage which the applicants maintain they sustained by reason of the manner in which the Commission dealt with their complaints,
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
1. Dismisses as inadmissible the claims for a declaration of an infringement;
2. Dismisses the claims for failure to act as inadmissible;

3. Annuls the contested decision in so far as it rejects Mr Cesbron's complaint of 18 November 1985 and the complaint of Mr Cesbron, Asia Motor France, Monnin Autobmobiles and EAS of 29 November 1988;
4. Dismisses the remainder of the claims for annulment as unfounded;
5. Dismisses the claims for damages as inadmissible;

6. Dismisses as unfounded the claims that the Commission should be ordered to pay the costs of the proceedings which culminated in the judgment of the Court of First Instance of 29 Jue 1993 in Case T-7/92 Asia Motor France and Others v Commisssion (1993) ECR II-669;
7. Orders the Commission to bear its own costs and to pay half the applicants' costs.
